title: New class fed-vortex: in a gravity-free 2D fluid where vorticity grows only by eating a regrowing fuel, vortex spots form from random vorticity, and a +/- pair travels as a self-propelled dipole, swaps partners in a collision and runs on into fresh fuel while the abandoned vortex starves
summary: world.py is a 2D incompressible fluid (vorticity-streamfunction, periodic, no gravity, no imposed direction) with an ignition-like vorticity gain (k Y s - mu) omega, s = omega^2/(omega^2+wi^2), paid for by eating a diffusing, regrowing fuel at e Y s omega^2. From a random band-passed vorticity field the fuel flashes out and a few vortex spots (~100 px) survive in depletion halos; on seed 1 a + and a - spot lock into a dipole that translates by self-induction (25 px in 400 t), exchanges partner with a lone vortex at t~850, and the new dipole travels 50 px (about 5 sqrt(area)) into fresh fuel by t=1500 while the abandoned vortex shrinks from 118 to 57 px (dipole_seed1.json, sighting.png); seed 0 gives only same-sign monopoles, which merely orbit. The window is narrow: most of 20 settings (screen_notes.md) either flash out to nothing, blow up, or coarsen into domain-filling turbulence, and no division was seen. Motion here comes from the bodies' own pairing, not an external field, which is what the reacting thermals lack (20261027T0534-c53-audit-thermals).
